{#u0xu} # Discussion

{#mmvc} IR induces telomere dysfunction, resulting in the fusion of chromosome ends, ultimately leading to a catastrophic failure in cell mitosis. And this is a fundamental mechanism underlying the demise of solid tumor cells due to radiation exposure [@w:w20]. BIBR1532 emerges as a promising hTERT-specific active site inhibitor, capable of impairing DNA repair through the induction of telomere dysfunction. It effectively halts the growth of tumour cells both in vitro and in vivo thus enhances their susceptibility to ionizing radiation [@w:w21]. In our current investigation, we have observed that BIBR1532 significantly impedes the activation of the ATM/ATR-mediated DNA damage repair pathway subsequent to radiotherapy. This inhibition effect curbs the proliferation of tumour cells and restrains the growth of tumour volume. Furthermore, we have confirmed its radiosensitizing effect in the RT of NSCLC, both in vitro and in vivo. It’s noteworthy that in malignant solid tumors and hematological tumor cells the telomerase exhibits an increased activity under low-dose radiation conditions, but as the radiation doses rise, telomerase activity returns to baseline levels or even below baseline [@w:w22]. Consequently, the radiosensitizing influence of BIBR1532 on hypofractionated radiotherapy is not as conspicuous as that observed in conventional fractionated radiotherapy. BIBR1532 operates by cu

ops.markdown: More significantly, our study explores the impact and potential mechanism of low-dose BIBR1532 combined with radiotherapy on the TIME. BIBR1532 in RT activates the cGAS/STING signalling pathway, whereas BIBR1532 alone does not elicit this response. This activation augments cGAS sensitivity to cytoplasmic dsDNA, possibly reflecting the effect of BIBR1532 on telomerase activity. Notably, shortening of telomeres to a critical length involves a substantial time lag [@w:w24], whereas ionizing radiation (IR) directly breaks chromosomal DNA and generates substantial DSBs. The non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) pathway then rapidly repairs these DSBs, but this template-free mechanism may inadvertently generate structurally aberrant chromosomal fragments, which become improperly segregated and culminate in micronuclei [@w:w25]. Micronuclei could rupture the dsDNA and release it into the cytoplasm, thereby activating cGAS, which catalyses synthesis of cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP) and triggers the innate immune response [@w:w26]. Moreover, BIBR1532 intensifies IR-induced DNA damage, enhancing phosphorylation of STING, TBK1 and IRF3 in both tumour cells and dendritic cells (DCs), which increases interferon-beta (IFN-β) expression, fosters DC maturation and incites an anti-tumour immune response.
